newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 22.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The US President Bill Clinton has attacked the world of fashion, alleging that the use of stick-thin models who look like they are on heroin has glamourised the use of the drug. His comments follow the finding that there has been a big increase in heroin addiction in the States.
- RATES HANDOVER CUTS DEBT BILL BY MILLIONS

Gordon Brown's decision to transfer operational control of interst rates to the Bank of England is set to save the Exchequer over 85m stg this year and about 155m stg in 1998-1999. This is a result of the jump in gilt-edged stock prices which followed Brown's announcement on 6 May.
- ASHANTI GIVES GREEN LIGHT TO ANGLO MOVE

The Ghanaian gold mining group Ashanti Goldfields has said it will not raise objections to the possible 2bn stg merger between Lonrho and JCI, despite one consequence of the merger being Anglo American of South Africa becoming a major shareholder in the group. According to JCI's proposals, Anglo would take Lonrho's 33 percent stake in Ashanti if the deal was completed.
- GREENBACK RALLIES AS JAPAN APPLIES BRAKES

The dollar continued to bounce back from the five-month low it hit during Tuesday's Far East trading. Japanese officials concluded the greenback had fallen far enough, and it recovered to 115.38 yen today.
